name: Sable Noir Cardamom-Rose Tablets
description: Thin, snappable tablets made from premium cacao-adjacent synth-base — not real chocolate, but engineered to behave like 72% dark — pressed with cardamom oil and dried rosewater crystals. Each foil-wrapped tablet is embossed with a geometric pattern.
flavor_profile: Deep, slightly bitter synth-cacao with genuine cardamom warmth and a floral rose finish that doesn't tip into perfume; clean snap, long melt
slogan: Close enough to remember. Good enough to forget the difference.
cultural_context: Sable Noir is aspirational — Tier 3 consumers buy it to feel Tier 4, and Tier 4 consumers buy it when real chocolate feels excessive. The slogan is considered slightly melancholy by design. Gift-giving is a primary purchase driver.
story_hooks: A Sable chemist has quietly cracked a synth-cacao formula that is, by blind taste test, indistinguishable from real chocolate — the corponation suppressing this data is the same one that controls real cocoa futures.
A character receives a Sable Noir tablet as a gift with a message embossed into the pattern using a custom mold — it's a code, and decoding it requires knowing who sent it.
Sable is running a quiet promotion where one tablet per production run contains a real cacao inclusion — finding it has become an obsessive game in Tier 3 social circles.
